pages.title: Enzyme Inhibition
pages.text: $(thing)Enzyme Inhibition$()$(br2)A molecule that sits in the enzyme's pocket without reacting slows it down; more substrate can push it out. How most drugs work. Unlocks a cheaper Stem Cell Culture.

$(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Enzyme Kinetics, The Steady-State Approximation.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Assayed Enzyme.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): An inhibitor at level I, with constant Q, sits in the enzyme's pocket and makes it seem to need more substrate. Write the apparent constant A, from the enzyme's own K.
